channel.description: Latest articles from Doug Casey’s International Man – Bias and Credibility (internationalman.com)

item.title: The Stupidest—and Potentially Most Dangerous—War Since 1945
item.description: The Iran war is the product of an embedded war apparatus, a recycled neocon script, and a political class that can’t say no. It’s barreling toward a disaster of historic proportions.

item.title: Going Down with the Ship
item.description: Why most people stay as freedoms erode—and how to build a lifeboat with a practical exit plan abroad.

item.title: Canada as the 51st State: The New Energy Geopolitics of the Western Hemisphere
item.description: A return to hard-power geopolitics in the Western Hemisphere—and what it means for energy security and markets.

item.title: Doug Casey on the Cost of the Iran War—and Why It Will Fuel Inflation
item.description: The Iran war is economically unsustainable, will accelerate debt monetization, and likely push inflation higher.

item.title: The Myth of Fed Independence—and How to Actually Stop the Inflation Machine
item.description: The Federal Reserve’s supposed independence has enabled a century of dollar debasement and asset bubbles, and that the real anti-inflation fix is to strip the Fed of its power.

item.title: All This Fuss About A Fiat Dollar
item.description: Fiat money repeatedly drives inflation and government controls, and early American history shows how a weakening dollar can lead to serious social and economic fallout.

item.title: The Uranium Setup That Made a Legend: A Market Built for 1,000%+ Moves
item.description: Uranium is a small market with big consequences: tight supply, rising reactor demand, and the recipe for violent repricings.

item.title: Doug Casey on The Real Causes of The American War of Secession
item.description: The American Civil War was shaped by slavery, tariffs, states’ rights, federal power, regional economic conflict, and British geopolitical pressure rather than a single-cause narrative.

item.title: The Super Bowl Top Signal
item.description: Today’s hottest trade may be far more fragile than investors think.

item.title: From Zimbabwe to Washington: The Farce of “Independent” Central Banks
item.description: A firsthand Zimbabwe hyperinflation case study shows how “independent” central banks ultimately become government financing tools—and why America is moving toward the same debt-driven endgame of money printing and escalating intervention.
